uncited: This family defines the primary objective functions for differentiable volume rendering, measuring the discrepancy between rendered images and ground-truth observations to drive gradient-based optimization.

It sets itself apart from sibling regularization losses (e.g., Total Variation, Eikonal) by focusing exclusively on pixel-level or perceptual fidelity rather than geometric constraints or smoothness priors.
All methods in this family compute a scalar loss $\mathcal{L}$ derived from the rendered color image $I_r$ (or $\hat{C}$) and the ground-truth image $I_{gt}$.
The core mechanism involves comparing these images using metrics such as L1, L2, SSIM, or LPIPS.
The total loss is typically a weighted sum of these fidelity terms and, in composite variants, auxiliary regularization terms defined in sibling articles.
Photometric losses are foundational to NeRF and Gaussian Splatting optimization.
